title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is a proposed law that seeks to protect the integrity of elections by regulating the use of artificial intelligence to create or spread misleading political content. It aims to require transparency and accountability for AI‑generated materials that could influence voters, helping to ensure that election results are based on accurate information.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives urges Congress to refuse additional funding or special regulatory relief for companies or financial institutions facing distress due to AI‑market exposures. Instead, it calls for support to be directed toward all Americans who have been adversely affected.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is intended to set clear standards and guidelines that make AI systems more trustworthy, safe, and reliable. It likely establishes oversight, transparency, and accountability mechanisms so researchers and developers must prove that their AI products perform consistently and ethically before they can be widely deployed.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 aims to make the use of artificial intelligence within the Department of Veterans Affairs clearer to veterans, healthcare providers, and regulators by requiring explicit disclosure of when and how AI systems are employed. The law also sets up reporting, documentation, and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI decisions are understandable, fair, and subject to accountability.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is proposed legislation designed to make sure that artificial intelligence used in handling veterans’ claims is transparent, fair, and subject to oversight. It sets out rules for how AI decisions should be documented, monitored, and corrected so veterans can challenge outcomes that may be unjust or biased.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act aims to safeguard consumers from misleading uses of artificial intelligence. It sets rules for transparency and accountability to prevent deceptive AI practices.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act proposes national standards and guidelines to ensure that advanced artificial intelligence systems are developed, deployed, and used securely. It focuses on protecting public safety by requiring thorough risk assessments, robust safeguards, and oversight to prevent misuse and harmful outcomes.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to address the security and resilience of artificial intelligence systems. The act aims to coordinate efforts between government agencies and private sector stakeholders to develop and implement policies that protect critical infrastructure from AI-related threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes a framework for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating risks associated with the use of artificial intelligence, ensuring that AI systems are designed and operated with safety and reliability in mind. The law sets mandatory security standards, oversight procedures, and compliance requirements for developers and users to protect public safety and prevent misuse of AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for overseeing the deployment, safety, and coordination of AI‑powered physical systems across various industries. It introduces regulatory standards, oversight mechanisms, and collaboration among government agencies to ensure responsible and secure integration of AI technology.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This act aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating the use of deceptive AI tools and requiring transparency about their deployment. It establishes safeguards, reporting requirements, and penalties to prevent manipulation of voters through AI-generated misinformation.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a legislative proposal aimed at regulating AI systems that can autonomously improve and change their own behavior. It would require such systems to be monitored, tested, and transparently reported on so that their development and operation remain safe and accountable.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to prevent artificial intelligence systems from acting in ways that could harm people or society. It would require companies to test and verify AI safety, make their processes transparent, and establish a government watchdog to enforce these rules.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction of new AI data centers to allow for a thorough assessment of their environmental and societal impacts. It aims to provide time for policymakers to evaluate and address potential risks before proceeding with large-scale AI infrastructure development.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to oversee and investigate cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence. It aims to strengthen national security by setting standards, coordinating responses, and ensuring accountability for AI‑related threats.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a proposal to ensure that artificial‑intelligence technologies developed and used in the United States directly benefit American citizens. It calls for responsible AI practices, safeguards for privacy, and support for innovation that strengthens the U.S. economy and society.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires Chinese AI developers and firms to submit detailed reports on their systems' capabilities, usage, and safety protocols. This legislation aims to increase transparency, promote responsible AI development, and enable government oversight of the sector.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 bars artificial intelligence from serving as the main provider of medical care, requiring that all patients be seen by licensed human doctors. It also mandates that any AI tools used in healthcare must be overseen and regulated by qualified medical professionals to ensure accountability and patient safety.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating a new office within the President’s Executive Office that will focus on monitoring and addressing risks from artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. It also outlines additional responsibilities for that office, though the specifics are not detailed in the title.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a new Select Committee dedicated to overseeing artificial intelligence. The committee will review AI developments, recommend policies, and advise lawmakers on related issues.
